title: Measurable Densities and Radon Volume on Manifolds

items.title: Pointwise Borel nonnegative densities
items.statement: Assume AC_omega throughout. M is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth n-manifold, with boundary allowed. A nonnegative Borel density has chart coefficients r_x:x(U)->[0,infinity], with r_x=(r_y composed with y composed with x inverse)|det D(y composed with x inverse)| pointwise. Extended coefficients are allowed; 0 times infinity is zero. For n=0 the empty determinant is one and lambda_0 assigns mass one to the singleton. This is an extended positive density cone, not an extended-valued section of the real line bundle. No a.e. identification is made.
items.proof_plan: The transition factors are finite strictly positive and Borel. The chain rule verifies consistency. A countable atlas suffices to test Borel coefficients; chart homeomorphisms preserve Borel sets. The scalar zero and empty manifold are included.

items.title: Agreement of Borel overlap integrals
items.statement: For every Borel E contained in two chart domains, the integrals of their nonnegative density coefficients over the two coordinate images of E agree in [0,infinity].
items.proof_plan: For n>=1 remove the face in each boundary chart; invariance of the boundary identifies the remaining open Euclidean sets. The indicator of the Borel coordinate image times the target coefficient is nonnegative Borel, so apply the preceding Radon-uniqueness C1 substitution lemma. The removed face has zero Lebesgue integral even for infinite coefficients. The n=0 assertion is equality of the same singleton weight. This local route does not invoke or repair the protected published measurable-C1 theorem.

items.title: Countable partition construction of the Borel set function
items.statement: For a countable locally finite chart cover U_i and subordinate nonnegative smooth partition phi_i define mu_r(A)=sum_i integral_{x_i(A intersect U_i)} (phi_i composed with x_i inverse)r_i d lambda_n for Borel A.
items.proof_plan: Choose a countable atlas with relatively compact chart pieces. For boundary charts use rational half-balls and the supplied boundary partition; aggregate terms assigned to each member of the countable refinement. Extend each weighted coefficient by zero only as a Borel function. This construction uses countable choice, not arbitrary simultaneous chart choices.

items.title: The glued set function is a Borel measure
items.statement: The set function in the preceding definition is a countably additive nonnegative measure on B(M), without local integrability or sigma-finiteness assumptions on r.
items.proof_plan: Each chart summand is a measure pulled back through a Borel chart. For disjoint A_k exchange the two nonnegative countable sums by suprema of finite rectangular partial sums; Beppo Levi justifies each integral/sum interchange. Empty set has zero integral. Never apply sigma-finite product Tonelli to mu_r without proving sigma-finiteness.

items.title: Intrinsic density measure and its chart restriction
items.statement: All countable chart-partition constructions give the same measure mu_r. For any Borel E contained in a chart U, mu_r(E)=integral_{x(E)}r_x d lambda_n.
items.proof_plan: For two partitions expand each term using phi_i psi_j. These are nonnegative Borel weights on the countable common overlaps; transfer every term by the overlap lemma and exchange sums. For the chart restriction apply the same calculation with the indicator of E and sum phi_i=1. Do not assume compact support or finite total mass.

items.title: Positive smooth densities give Radon volume
items.statement: For a finite-valued positive smooth density r, mu_r is finite on compact sets, locally finite, sigma-finite, and a regular Borel (hence Radon) measure. Denote its completion by (M, completed B(M), completed mu_r); it is not identified with the Borel sigma-algebra.
items.proof_plan: Near each point shrink inside one chart to a compact coordinate ball or half-ball. The smooth coefficient is bounded there, so the chart restriction is finite. A compact set has a finite such cover. A countable cover proves sigma-finiteness. Half-ball closures prove LCH also at boundary points; Hausdorffness and second countability are standing hypotheses. Apply the precise compact-finite second-countable LCH regularity supplier, then the general completion theorem.

items.title: Borel Darboux integrands in finite dimension
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. If a bounded Borel real function on a nondegenerate compact n-box, n>=1, is Riemann integrable, its Lebesgue integral exists and equals its Riemann integral.
items.proof_plan: Shift by a constant to be nonnegative. For any rectangular partition make lower and upper Borel step functions from cell infima/suprema, disjointifying faces; their Lebesgue integrals are the Darboux sums because all faces are null. Squeeze the bounded measurable function between these step functions off the finite union of faces. The Darboux criterion makes the gap arbitrarily small. Subtract the shift. This explicit finite-dimensional adaptation is needed because the published comparison theorem only treats intervals.

items.title: Measurable integration extends smooth density integration
items.statement: For a nonnegative Borel f, integral_M f d mu_r equals sum_i integral_{x_i(U_i)} (phi_i f r)_i d lambda_n, allowing infinity. For positive smooth r and compactly supported smooth real f this is the existing smooth density integral of fr. Real and complex L1 functions have the corresponding absolutely convergent chart formula, and completed-measurable functions are treated through Borel representatives modulo completed null sets.
items.proof_plan: First prove the formula for indicators from the defining measure, then finite nonnegative simple functions, then increasing approximations. For smooth compact support only finitely many partition terms survive; each zero extension is bounded Borel and Riemann integrable on a box, so the new bridge identifies the two integrals. Split real and imaginary positive/negative parts only after integrating the absolute value. For completion replace completed simple sets by Borel sets modulo null sets, take a countable union of exceptional null sets, and pass to simple limits.

items.title: Positive open-set and metric-ball volume
items.statement: For positive smooth r every nonempty open subset of M has positive mu_r measure. For any metric inducing the topology, every ball B_d(p,R), R>0, is Borel and has positive measure; if its closure is compact its measure is finite.
items.proof_plan: Within the open set choose a smaller coordinate box where the positive continuous coefficient is bounded below. A relative boundary neighborhood contains an interior box in n>=1. In n=0 use a positive singleton weight. Topology-compatible balls are open and contain their center. Compact-finiteness gives the last clause; neither completeness nor curvature comparison is invoked.

items.title: False: locally finite volume has finite total mass
items.statement: The assertion that every positive smooth density on a manifold has finite total mass is false.
items.proof_plan: On R with density |dx|, the interval [-N,N] has measure 2N. Every compact set is bounded and has finite mass, whereas the supremum over N is infinite.

items.title: False: density measures require an orientation
items.statement: It is false that nonorientable manifolds cannot carry positive smooth density measures.
items.proof_plan: Use the explicit Mobius strip seam from the existing A-page refutation: (s,t)->(s+1,-t) has absolute determinant one, so |ds dt| glues. Its sign-changing determinant prevents an orientation, while the positive density gives a measure.

title: Measurable Densities and Radon Volume on Manifolds: Examples

items.title: Euclidean volume from chart gluing
items.statement: On R^n, n>=1, the standard density |dx| gives Borel Lebesgue measure; its completion is ordinary Lebesgue measure.
items.proof_plan: Use the identity chart and partition one in the chart restriction formula. For a box compute the product of side lengths.

items.title: Weighted interval volume
items.statement: On (0,1), r=x^-1|dx| gives mu_r((a,b))=log(b/a) for 0<a<b<1, finite mass on compact subsets and infinite total mass.
items.proof_plan: Integrate 1/x on each compact subinterval using the published logarithmic primitive and the finite-box Riemann/Lebesgue bridge. Exhaust (0,1) by [1/N,1-1/N], N>=3, and apply monotone convergence; log(N-1) tends to infinity.

items.title: Circle overlap weights count each arc once
items.statement: On S^1=R/(2 pi Z), take the angular charts (-pi,pi) and (0,2 pi), each with density coefficient one. Their transitions are translations by 0 or 2 pi. Any subordinate partition gives total mass 2 pi.
items.proof_plan: On the two overlap components explicitly insert phi_1+phi_2=1; transfer by translations. Split into the disjoint semicircles (0,pi), (pi,2 pi) and the two endpoints. Each endpoint has zero measure by the chart restriction, so the sum is 2 pi.

items.title: Flat Mobius strip density measure
items.statement: On the open Mobius strip (R times (-1,1))/((s,t)~(s+1,-t)), the Euclidean quadratic form ds^2+dt^2 and the density |ds dt| descend. The density is the one taking value one on orthonormal frames of this explicit metric; the total volume is 2.
items.proof_plan: Reuse the A-page strip seam construction, not an examples-page dependency. The seam transition has matrix diag(1,-1); compute determinant absolute value one and invariance of the quadratic form. A fundamental strip [0,1) times (-1,1) has area 2; seam has zero volume. Prove the orthonormal-frame normalization directly from absolute determinants. No future DG-18 Riemannian-density theorem is used.

items.title: Weighted counting in dimension zero
items.statement: For a second-countable zero-manifold M and nonnegative weights w(p), mu_w(A)=sum_{p in A}w(p). Positive finite weights give a Radon measure; total mass need not be finite.
items.proof_plan: Singletons are open; injection into a countable base makes M countable. Choose singleton charts and their indicator partition, whose functions are smooth in dimension zero. Compact subsets of a discrete space are finite. For M=N and w(k)=2^(-k-1) total mass is one; weights one give infinite mass.

items.title: A smooth positive density with infinite mass
items.statement: Euclidean density on R is a counterexample to finite total mass of a positive smooth density measure.
items.proof_plan: Compute mu([-N,N])=2N and let N grow; compact sets remain finite. This is the required concrete B-page witness, independent of the A-page logical refutation.

items.title: Metric balls need no curvature comparison for measurability
items.statement: On (0,1) with Euclidean distance and density x^-1|dx|, B(1/2,1/4) has volume log 3; B(1/2,1) is all of (0,1) and has infinite volume.
items.proof_plan: The first ball is (1/4,3/4) with compact closure inside the manifold; the second is the whole manifold, so it is not relatively compact. Both are open Borel sets. This shows why the finite-volume qualifier cannot be omitted.
